1:א: There is Taz nevertheless section 17 from chapter 5 of Shabbat law 9 see there, and siman 345 in Magen Avraham section 1 — dispute of Rambam and other poskim; and nevertheless lechi is because of partition d'oraisa and korah is because of recognition, and Eruvin 12 — a mavo they qualified with lechi — one who throws into it is liable, with korah exempt according to Rambam; it will be explained with three partitions and to explain poskim with two partitions; and Eruvin section 17 here, and nevertheless there lechi is d'oraisa and korah is the issue; and see Levush here; and practical difference to disqualify testimony or a mumar who desecrates Shabbat d'oraisa is a mumar — so it is; however some say we have no reshut ha-rabbim — siman 345 in Taz section 6:
1:ב: The simpleton said who writes on the law of lavud and tzurat hapetach — I have thoughts on the matter and I set them forth here with God's help. Know that lavud is nevertheless, and even two lavud above and below, and even in length we say lavud; and in explanation of lavud — not that which they say as closed; nevertheless for lechi distant from the wall less than 3 tefachim Magen Avraham section 5 — rather even if we say that in any case air is as closed, as in seif 35 and three ropes etc. siman 362 — behold there is height ten; Rashi Sukkah 4b s.v. less than etc. that they extend etc.; and behold in lavud nevertheless it is a complete partition for all its matters and from the conditions of lavud in 14 seif 1 — Rambam wrote in the gloss that one cannot say lavud to be stringent see there; in Magen Avraham siman 372 letter 9 he expanded on this and brought s.v. Eruvin 10 see there; and in siman 632 — or section 5 — explanation of what Tur wrote that we do not say lavud to be stringent, that it is like adjacent — do not err to explain his words as lavud like adjacent, for we hold lavud as extending and as closed by here; rather to say lavud entirely to be stringent like closed; and in invalid s'chach we do not say except like closed extending and not in invalid s'chach; but in beit 19 invalid s'chach and another 19 invalid between them air less than 3 tefachim — I have to doubt whether lavud whether we also say as adjacent and invalid, or only as extending and closed and we say as closed in valid see there; and see Levush; and behold if we say lavud as actual substance to say as if it is not — the matter inquired in Sukkah 4b and below in chapter 5 Sukkah 632 seif 10 — he carved up to ten less than 3 tefachim to the wall — we say lavud; and Rashi: the carving as if it reaches the wall — behold lavud as actual substance; and one may say this is dispute in Tur there Magen Avraham there section 8 whether valid from carving to wall — one may say lavud as if the partition seals the air over the carving, not the ground between them as removed — understand. And responsum Chatam Sofer section 59 in small gardens wrote lavud as actual substance we do not say; and proof invalid s'chach that between them is valid less than 3 tefachim — we do not say lavud as if the valid were removed in actual substance see there; and this is in 632 seif 4 specifically air between them; and one may say that whenever there is valid between them entirely we do not say lavud to be stringent — see Levush there. And what he wrote there proof from Eruvin 25a — partition adjacent to partition less than 3 tefachim as lavud — therefore lavud to be stringent — one may say not from lavud theory but it is annulled and not considered; Rashi there made as if; and there are poskim like Rav Shimi bar Ashi even though we do not hold so. And in siman 345 less than 3 tefachim lavud implies even in actual substance — see there in urine and feces and in that of Shabbat 7 threw and did not land on anything less than 3 tefachim etc.; and therefore lechi distant less than 3 tefachim from the wall and between them a board of asherah wood — some say invalid, for it is actual substance; and even though burned it counts for measure nevertheless it is actual substance that we do not say lavud; and Magen Avraham here section 5 and 631 Taz section 2 — if so if asherah wood stands there it is worse still; and all the more here letter 8 and Magen Avraham 626 section 6. And behold lavud is a complete partition nevertheless to obligate one who throws there, and also for leniency; and from rabbanan it is called inferior as in siman 304 Magen Avraham section 2; and one may say the stringency of two without eruv, or the reverse — for all that have two and eruv one may say even if he drove stakes less than 3 tefachim and one reed on top of them alone for eruv — it is an excellent partition, and even more than beit se'atayim; and in encirclement and eruv alone like those fifteen attached to pegs in four bundles — requires study. Siman 358 section 6 in Levush — lavud to reduce air more than 3 tefachim we do not say; and see there:
1:ג: Tzurat hapetach — its law is explained in 362 seif 10; and here section 26 — and it implies even if made from asherah wood it is valid, for the measure of lechi is not required; and what requires d'oraisa — hard and ashes are not fit for that — nevertheless permitted; and all the more letter 9 he brought s.v. on ladder of asherah; and it will be explained below. And all the more in siman 362 letter 25 whether d'oraisa is required in tzurat hapetach — and it will be explained there in Taz letter 19. And know that I am in doubt in tzurat hapetach whether it is partition d'oraisa to obligate one who throws within when driving four pegs and upon them tzurat hapetach — then tzurat hapetach helps to permit karmelit; and a breach more than ten amot — nevertheless it is partition from something — tzurat hapetach helps; and siman 631 sections 62 and 63 imply tzurat hapetach alone does not help for sukkah; and in section 26 he drove four pegs — implies even if he placed a reed above them it does not help; and Magen Avraham letter 9 — any mashehu is partition in sukkah helps etc. — it appears tzurat hapetach does not help except for karmelit and the like — not to be complete reshut ha-yachid through tzurat hapetach; and requires much study. Siman 358 in water — does not make a petach — one may say tzurat hapetach does not help there whenever wider than 3 tefachim; and siman 361 in Magen Avraham section 4; and all the more here in tzurat hapetach whether we require width of 4 tefachim or even less — and it will be explained there in Taz letter 19 further:
2:_: Courtyard — Taz: the difference between mavo and courtyard — siman 362 and mavo — for it is permitted with lechi or korah many conditions are required; but in courtyard, whenever its length is greater than its width — with this condition alone lechi or korah suffices; siman 362; and therefore he set the difference of square in courtyard:
3:_: Tefach — Taz: explanation of the Mechaber's words that he retracted here from what he wrote in Beit Yosef and holds that in what remains in the wall we require a tefach from here and from here, as in seif 4 in lechi in the wall — 4 are required a tefach; and in Levush he wrote here two mashehuyin; and likewise Be'er Heitev section 5 implies his view is so; but in truth requires study, for Beit Yosef in his long book brought Tosafos 10a s.v. "and two" and brought it in seif 4 in lechi — and from there he learned it; and Tosafos in courtyard wrote their words — if so, courtyard also requires two tefachim; and see in section 2; and again I saw in Tosafos Shabbos letter 4 he stood on this:
4:_: Therefore — Taz: his view in tzurat hapetach — plaster smearing and coating on the wall helps, and it should be somewhat thick and protruding, and a reed above; but lechi alone without tzurat hapetach — plaster smearing and protrusion do not help, for measure of something is required. And in Ateret Zekenim letter 9 he wrote for Beit Yosef — in lechi too any amount see there; Magen Avraham section 2; and in responsum Teshuvot HaDavar siman 74 it is explained so — lechi according to one view like a finger does not help with plaster smearing; but for the Mechaber in section 63 it helps; and in section 26 requires study; and it will be explained there:
5:_: From wood — Taz: all that stands to be scattered is as scattered; except Tosafos section 1 — the essence according to the Mechaber in section 62 in any case all the more; and a finger is not required in plainness; and height ten tefachim — no question; see Be'er Heitev letter 70; and see Tosafos Shabbos letter 13 — he brought Tosafos Eruvin chapter 2 s.v. "but" see there. And behold it implies anything mashehu requires measure like shofar and lulav in its length even though in width there is no measure — invalid like cut pieces etc.; and so too from rabbanan requires measure in length alone, like high nineteen they were not stringent; and korah from rabbanan requires width of a tefach — even from rabbanan disqualifies; and lulav on 19 — second in the mitzvah they were stringent see there in Tosafos. However there is to doubt in a matter mashehu that requires measure in height — whether nevertheless invalid in cut pieces, or only from rabbanan; and practical difference — two partitions and lechi of asherah wood such a case — Magen Avraham section 1; and in section 2 one may say mashehu (1) and all the more here letter 13; and see Even HaEzer 124 and Choshen Mishpat section 1; and in section 2 one may say — the question of Choshen Mishpat how he wrote the get in 39 implies entirely — one may say all that stands to be burned is as burned only for stringency and not for leniency see there. And siman 506 section 63 and 639 section 63 — mitzvot are not for benefit were given even in rabbinic mitzvah; and such a case is considered a mitzvah even though movable from words of Torah; unlike in 72 section 66 — ladder of asherah forbidden to climb see there; and Magen Avraham letter 7; and it will be explained there:
6:_: Between — Taz in Eruvin 70b — and it appears "equal outside" — all agree it is lechi; and "appears outside and equal inside" — there is dispute; and the halacha is they are lechayim; and "between between" that the Mechaber set — for according to the majority, between-between is this one, and a fortiori this one as what Semag wrote in Choshen Mishpat 72 letter 8; and if so it should have said here first "between appears outside" and "between appears inside" is judged because of lechi; but since in the Gemara this matter is set first "appears inside" etc. — and it is possible to impose this on Taz; and nevertheless it is difficult — it should have said the wording of Tur see there. (What Semag wrote there that the Mechaber explained "equal outside-inside" not to reduce, for it is not like asking — and therefore there letter 9; and in Klalim in the opening of the book we wrote from this.) And what Taz wrote in diagrams 70 Gemara and in Maharshal and Perishah — he expanded here and there was no time to study it properly:
7:_: If — Taz and likewise Magen Avraham letter 11 — whatever the lechi length is four amot, which is the qualification of mavo as in seif 26, and stands in the width of the mavo — leaning does not help see there; and even if he placed lechi not for the sake of permitting mavo and leaned afterward — it is nothing; only in the initial making from the start intent is required to permit; and the gloss: but if he leaned it — it should be in seif 11 here — leaning does not help as stated. See letter 13:
8:_: Lechi — Taz and likewise Magen Avraham letter 14 — that here even if fixed for the sake of lechi it is forbidden; for regarding width, because they closed it more — they did not reduce; however there we require at least that it was fixed. And what is written here implies we do not hold like Tosafos; and all the more letter 27 he brought Ra'osh's words see there — he left requires study:
9:_: And it is required — Taz: in the edition we marked in section 64, and it should be in section 66 — lechi standing by itself is lechi because of partition, and korah by itself is not korah, for for recognition we require that it was fixed for that purpose; and in seif 64 the reason that we require korah over the mavo and there is none — like Rava Eruvin 8b; and see Beit Yosef — the halacha is like Rava; and if so it is permitted to use beneath the korah — if so according to those who permit it is forbidden; and it is possible open to karmelit; and siman 364 seif 4 — and it implies he placed two pegs inside the mavo and korah on them — permitted even for Rava; and likewise seif 21 placed on the pillars — namely in a manner that the pillars are not judged because of lechi; and likewise what the Mechaber wrote a fortiori the mavo; and see Olat Shabbat on this. And siman 388:
10:_: That there is not — Taz: behold those who place korah in Eruvin 17a — dispute there; and it can be explained plainly — he drove two pegs straight on top of the wall at its head and placed the korah on them; and the diagram the Mechaber wrote is what is in the Gemara 9a — Rav Ashi said two pegs bent — and that is below in seif 25; and the diagram in the Gemara there see there as Rashi explained — it teaches us throw down and lavud; Magen Avraham letter 21; and it will be explained there; and on this the Mechaber wrote here a novelty — even though the essence of leaning the korah on the pegs is toward the side of the mavo — nevertheless some say it is not required in those who support the korah except to receive the korah alone; and see Beit Yosef:
11:_: That it requires — Taz: Beit Yosef challenged — plainly reed is invalid, for it cannot receive a brick see there; and Taz: reed is not broken in weaving if a brick was placed on it except that it bent and folded; and it came below ten literally — therefore invalid; what the Mechaber wrote in seif 20 bent Eruvin 14a see there:
12:_: Within — Taz: Magen Avraham 18; and see Beit Yosef — it appears for the reason that here there is no measure — two korot touching one another literally are required; if separated even less than a tefach — forbidden, for here there is no measure; but Taz explains that there is no measure means one cannot lean half a brick on them:
13:_: Somewhat — Taz and Magen Avraham letter 20; and the principle is — korah that one placed below nineteen or above twenty amot is invalid; however a very thick and wide korah that one placed and its upper head above nineteen — even though it is wide and reaches the ground below nineteen — it is valid, since the upper head is above nineteen; for here it is better than seif 20 — we view what is within nineteen as if they are not — it teaches us the Mechaber: if it is very wide and has approximately nineteen in it and is placed entirely above nineteen — it has not left the category of korah even though it has width of nineteen like a partition; for above nineteen there is no law of partition — even if its width reaches below nineteen and more than 3 tefachim to the ground — if so it left the category of korah and is disqualified; and partition it is not, for more than 3 tefachim to the ground; and on this Rashba disagrees — it teaches us the Mechaber it is valid; and what he wrote from 362 letter 7 — if made for lechi even protruding four amot valid in lechi; and what he wrote korah — see letter 27 — in lechi recognition like korah is not required see there. And know that in seif 62 in lechi drawn along the width of the mavo — it is difficult from seif 4 — who is worse in a wall in a fourth wind? One may say since the mavo was initially breached in its entirety and he made correction with lechi four amot long and not with intent — it is not permitted thereby until it stands with intent:
14:_: Spaced — Taz in all the laws — even of scribes here we go stringently; wherever nineteen is required we require spaced; and wherever disqualified in more than ten amot and the like — also precise disqualifies; and see Olat Shabbat; and one may say there is still one doubt — whether they combine for two pasin — requires study:
15:_: It is not — Taz and see letter 29 — korah four tefachim wide descends and closes in air wider than ten; and also "the eye rules over it" see there; and it appears an error in what he wrote seven — only four see there; and nevertheless in 366 in Magen Avraham section 5 — four tefachim even in more than ten helps — requires study. And lechi helps at height more than twenty, for it is partition; and see Bach seif 64 — lechi equal inside and outside is not judged because of lechi unless it protrudes somewhat higher than the walls of the mavo; and such a case — all that height above five amot there is no recognition even though lechi is partition nevertheless recognition is also required see there; and Tosafos Shabbos letter 53 brought it; and it will be explained there in letter 19 further:
16:_: Requires — Taz: Rashi Eruvin 5a s.v. Rav Yosef; and see Levush; and behold it implies building width of a tefach like the width of the korah, and according to the entire width of the mavo that building; and in carving according to the entire width of the mavo in length four amot; and siman 631 in Magen Avraham section 8 — less than 3 tefachim to the side is valid; and if so here one may say whatever is less than 3 tefachim in the width of the mavo for two walls and less than 3 tefachim in length four amot to the wall — it should be valid; and if we say carving as if the air were closed from the side — if so here too; and it depends on the dispute whether carving is as actual substance etc. — see what is written in Taz section 1; and in the dispute of Tur in 631 see there — understand:
17:_: And there is — Taz: in the corrected edition nevertheless as fitting; and Magen Avraham letter 27 on this; and it will be explained there:
18:_: And there is — Taz as above in seif 2 line 4 — or two lines mashehuyin on each side one of them. And behold our towns that are not surrounded by a wall that have breaches between house and house — they are not in their entirety according to the majority, only a breach more than ten amot; if so it is impossible with line four, only with tzurat hapetach as in seif 2 see there; and a breach that is like ten amot — no correction is required at all, since it is not breached in its entirety as in seif 2 see there; and it will be explained in letter 19 some correction for our towns and the law of tzurat hapetach and lechi and line four; and here there is no place to expand:
19:א: And therefore — Taz: siman 362 in Taz section 4 and Magen Avraham letter 19 — implies one must beware in such a case because of the viewer; and what he wrote that we conclude in the Gemara Eruvin 11b regarding a dome — and what he wrote that the roof must not interrupt; and all the more letter 64 challenged him from Eruvin 11b dome proves the interruptor does not ruin; and Yoreh De'ah 287 section 3 challenged him see there; behold in Yoreh De'ah there in letter 2 — for Rambam another approach in Eruvin and Yoma 11b; see Be'er Heitev there; and nevertheless Peri Chadash from what he wrote here that for Rambam whatever is not in a flat mezuzah nineteen high — if so the circle — which will you make of them mezuzah and which the arch, or all mezuzah there is no lintel, or all lintel there is no height nineteen; and he does not hold carving; unlike when there is in the flat twenty-nine — then the entire arch is considered lintel; and what is in the Gemara Eruvin and Yoma 11b "without width of four" — and there is to carve four tefachim — a novelty he said even without width of four in the circle, all that can carve four tefachim Rambam holds carving; but if there is no carving four tefachim — Rabbenu Tam also agrees there is no carving to complete height ten; and for the Rabbis in every case all that has mezuzah height straight nineteen is obligated even though there is no width of four at all; and when there is not height nineteen straight even though there is width of four in the circle itself — nevertheless which will you make mezuzah and which lintel; and one may say how did he say support that tzurat hapetach in reeds is not required for Rambam; and for Rashi properly from height nineteen etc.; unlike for Rambam height nineteen of the circle immediately becomes lintel; and there is to reject and say from Rambam he brings proof to say carving and as if touching actually we do not say; and therefore one may say the Rabbis do not hold so; and in truth Rif and Ra'osh — halacha is like Rabbenu that taught thus — we publicize not like Rambam's explanation; and nevertheless Peri Chadash from what he wrote here nineteen — halacha is like Rabbenu — he did not conclude "taught thus"; and with this one may say Taz's words what requires a hole in the roof — understand; and there is no place to expand:
19:ב: The simpleton said who writes on the law of tzurat hapetach — there is to investigate. (1) The upper reed if it is above twenty amot and air of twenty between the reeds and that which is tied to a roof very high — what is the law. (2) Tzurat hapetach that he distanced from the side 3 tefachim — what is the law. (3) Partitions that are not height nineteen — whether tzurat hapetach helps. (4) Tzurat hapetach made from the side in 362 — whether specifically from the side — for it is inserted between reed and reed and carved somewhat in the reeds as craftsmen do — even though the reeds protrude above also, it is possible it is permitted; behold in Bach it implies permitted in tzurat hapetach even though the upper reed is above twenty between it and the reeds beneath; and all the more on this; and tzurat hapetach that he distanced 3 tefachim from the wall of the reeds — Magen Avraham section 5 — for Tosafos implies forbidden; and also in Biur Halacha one may say forbidden; and all the more in the name of Tevu'at Shor from this; and partitions that are not height nineteen — in Shulchan Aruch here in section 26 it is explained that tzurat hapetach helps for low partitions less than nineteen — whenever tzurat hapetach is height nineteen; and requires study in siman 345 that all that are low less than nineteen is karmelit; and all the more letter 51; and in Rambam section 17 from what he wrote fourteen — they disagreed on him and hold all whose partitions are less than nineteen tzurat hapetach does not help; and see Beit Yosef what he wrote and so wrote Rashba — it must be; and it is not Rashba's view; and requires study — one may say what is written in Shulchan Aruch "less than nineteen" is at the place of the opening — for all listed there are three partitions height nineteen, otherwise it is like karmelit as a house whose interior is not nineteen in siman 345 — requires study; and siman 362 in Taz letter 4 what he wrote from the side; and see Hagahot Alfasi Eruvin 11 — and not that it be inserted between both in its middle — implies it must rest on the head of the reeds; however driving a nail in the heads of the reeds and wrapping rope on them helps as above; and what Taz wrote wrappings protrude until nineteen near the ground — it appears proper to emend 3 tefachim near the ground; see seif 10 in lechi; and all the more letter 11 and letter 64 — wrappings not for tzurat hapetach, for it is petachei Shammai Eruvin 11a petachei Shammai; and Yoreh De'ah 287 see there in Taz — requires study; and therefore wrappings in a wooden wall called Wängel and the like — requires study in this; and tzurat hapetach that between reed and reed is not four tefachim — all the more 362 letter 25 for Rambam tzurat hapetach in less than width four tefachim helps; and for Tur we require four like mezuzah; and nevertheless section 17 section 20; and see seif 28 in any case all that the opening of the mavo is not width four amot — for Rambam tzurat hapetach helps; and for Ra'osh correction is not required except when very wide and made many tzurat hapetach that are not width four tefachim, or open such a case; and there is to see if open and the opening is not width four tefachim — whether its law is as open:
19:ג: And know that dome is mentioned in 362 seif 12 — and for Rambam and Rashi like dispute in mezuzah — likewise here; and one may say for the Rabbis in dome all that is less than 3 tefachim of the mezuzah of seven amot — why do we not say carving as in siman 631; and Magen Avraham section 8 there whether the carving reaches the wall, or we say as one who fills until the groove — if so:
19:ד: If tzurat hapetach was ruined on Shabbat — whether we say since it was permitted it was permitted — Magen Avraham letter 4; and what I wrote there; and in siman 374 implies specifically courtyard to courtyard — but to another domain we do not say since it was permitted it was permitted; and Magen Avraham letter 27; and it will be explained there in 374 from this; and if on Yom Tov it was ruined — whether we say since it was permitted where it is fit to say since it was permitted — it will also be explained there; and here there is no place to expand:
20:_: Perhaps — Taz: in a city surrounded by a river high whose banks are nineteen — it is partition; and they acquired from the lord as in siman 382 — not to forbid gentiles — he raised it is forbidden; and he brought Gemara Eruvin 8a — prohibition he did not say because partitions stand; and he raised even on other days of the year in summer forbidden to carry in the city on the river see there; behold the river — in winter when the waters freeze and it is possible more frequent than the sea sandbar of thirty-nine for one view — unlike here; however if there is a place of slope it is permitted etc.; and in Magen Avraham 41 in the name of nevertheless implies even if there is a place of slope it is forbidden see there; and Taz holds even for nevertheless all that there is a place of slope — earth that collects nineteen within four amot is permitted; and Magen Avraham in winter days forbids and in summer days perhaps permits; and it will be explained there; however in other rivers for sandbar we are not concerned; and therefore he permitted in beit tel etc. Magen Avraham. And behold in concern of sandbar one may say rabbinically thirty-nine likewise unlike frozen and many pass there — it is actual reshut ha-rabbim — there is to decree more; and see in siman 345 Taz section 6 and Magen Avraham section 7 that they are lenient to say nowadays it is karmelit; and nevertheless with the view of Rambam here one may say. And behold one may say what Rashi wrote sandbar like width of a parsah as nevertheless explained and they would carry — and there in the sea and it is enclosed not for dwelling as Magen Avraham wrote letter 41; and Marimar who ruled in Uzla — one may say he holds properly we are not concerned for sandbar lest they carry from mavo to sandbar, for they were not accustomed to that and it would not come to that; unlike within the city they would carry as initially — we are concerned properly etc.; and Sura had no slope nineteen along four amot and he was concerned properly lest they carry in the city as initially — and he ruled in Uzla; and therefore how it will be in any case when there is slope it is permitted; and this that Taz brought nevertheless's explanation and Rashi like width of parsah — for a specific intent he brought thus and as stated; and it will be explained further in Magen Avraham. And see responsum Knesset Yechezkel siman 2 and other simanim — he expanded here see there; and Magen Avraham 365 letter 9; and see here letter 35; and regarding a city surrounded by a deep ditch nineteen high and width four tefachim — it is complete partition to permit the city — responsum Chatam Sofer section 5 section 6; and see siman 374 in Magen Avraham letter 29 — all that the width of the ditch is less than four tefachim it is easy to step over and is not partition for the city; and if there are bridges wider than nineteen — tzurat hapetach specifically is required; and it will be explained in 365 in Magen Avraham; and here there is no place to expand; and know that a river surrounding or a tel surrounding a city is karpef more than beit se'atayim — Magen Avraham letter 38 letter 20 — rather one may say when there are bridges wider than ten amot the partition around the city is annulled; and afterward when he made tzurat hapetach at the place of the bridge as in siman 358 section 62 — it is enclosed except for the reason of roofing; and therefore in a place where the bridge is not width ten amot in any case forbidden to carry in the city; and it will be explained further in Magen Avraham:
21:_: But — Taz: Eruvin 8b implies even if he wishes to use only opposite the short side — nevertheless they do not place the korah diagonally lest they err and use opposite the long against the long; and also there is not so much recognition when placed diagonally; and further that korah over the walls of the mavo is required, and in length it is not over the walls of the mavo — forbidden to use there; and this is what Rava said — he places only opposite the short, and he did not say he uses only opposite the short — if so for Tosafos section 1 s.v. "places" — for Rava why do I need the reason that there is no recognition — it should suffice that there are no partitions; and see Tosafos Shabbos they brought it. And what Taz wrote section 15 — it appears within the mavo even diagonally permitted — namely when in the diagonal there is not more than ten; and you saw that more than ten — even for Rav Kahana forbidden — likewise for Rava within the mavo such a case (and the words "except diagonally" must be emended — and the reading: rather requires ten precise and not more) — and with this what Rif wrote more than ten — all agree dispute is only within the mavo as stated; and see Beit Yosef; and Taz wrote that from the Mechaber's and Tur's wording it implies within the mavo even if there is more than ten in the diagonal permitted to place the korah diagonally — for otherwise he should have said first within the mavo permitted diagonally and afterward written tzurat hapetach permitted opposite long and short; and nevertheless they are not equal — for korah within the mavo like the width of the opening of the mavo more than ten amot certainly does not help even when the walls of the mavo are equal; and tzurat hapetach helps only when more than ten is in the diagonal that within the mavo with korah is permitted; and all the more. And two lechayim he wrote there is no doubt at all — certainly it permits only opposite the short when placing them at the end of the mavo — not like Bach; and Magen Avraham letter 32; and what he wrote that opposite it is reshut ha-rabbim — one may say lechi is partition and there are three partitions from the long side and the breach in a fourth wind is not in its entirety; and all the more for karmelit such a case; and nevertheless one may say even open to karmelit two lechayim diagonally do not help — for the short lechi is as if partition there opposite it straight, and further there is no permission at all opposite the long lechi; and see letter 23:
22:_: If — Taz: behold he placed lechi in the middle of the mavo — namely in the middle of the wall and adjacent to the wall less than 3 tefachim as explained; and all that the outer ones also made lechi for the remaining mavo and they can make eruv together — then they forbid one another even though the outer ones have no treading of foot on the inner ones — for it is like a city of an individual that became of the many since they were accustomed to make eruv together; see Beit Yosef in the name of Ra'osh; and it appears to me even if they did so initially — each placed one lechi for itself and they were never accustomed to make eruv together — nevertheless since most mavo'ot are accustomed thus to make eruv together — all the mavo is likewise; and so too somewhat in Levush; and if the outer ones have no lechi — they do not forbid the inner ones since the outer ones are not fit to make eruv; and it appears even if the outer ones have treading of foot on the inner ones such a case where they did not make lechi — they do not forbid the inner ones; unlike when the residents divided with pasin or tzurat hapetach and the outer ones did not make eruv — if the outer ones have treading of foot they forbid the inner ones; and if they have no treading of foot they do not forbid; see Beit Yosef; and Tosafos Shabbos; and what the Mechaber wrote in 362 — and all this when there is qualification of mavo — namely he placed lechi in half the mavo and not outside; and nevertheless section 17 section 20 refers above — for they also made outer ones and made eruv — the mavo combines together whenever there are between them all two courtyards — permitted; but in tzurat hapetach two pasin — I am in doubt if in the outer part there are not two courtyards whether they are permitted — requires study:
23:_: But — Taz: one courtyard itself can divide with tzurat hapetach or two pasin; see Beit Yosef; and Magen Avraham; and see Eruvin 14b — half a mavo has half a mavo — plainly; and one may say perhaps it came to teach us that the outer ones do not forbid it when they did not make lechi even though they have treading of foot; and one may say it is preferable to the second; and one may say let us say it has only half as initially that requires two courtyards etc.; and one may say:
24:_: And when he places — Taz: and even though it is breached more than standing in a fourth wind and also the air of this side and that side is greater — since there is length four amot in the pas it is like a mavo whose measure is mavo length — and therefore it is like two mavo'ot; unlike in 364 the pas is not width four amot except because it reduces the opening of the mavo from twenty amot; and in Magen Avraham it will be explained further:
25:_: All — Taz: and see seif 26 laws of conditions of mavo:
26:_: And what — Taz: in 364 bent mavo like a gimmel or like a chet is like open even though there is not width ten amot between reshut ha-rabbim and karmelit or in its bends; and here Ra'osh wrote specifically when there is more than ten amot from the pas until the middle wall (until three partitions and a fourth wind open in the east he places in the east pas four one; and if from the pas until the western wall more than ten amot etc. — tzurat hapetach is required as in 364); and Taz wrote that here it is not literally like bent mavo; and one may say we view as if the place from the pas goes straight until the western wall — and two mavo'ot are on the side of this pas and on the side of the two they also go equally and straight — and in neither is open; unlike when there is more than ten amot from the pas until the western wall — if so there is no opening between the middle mavo and the mavo'ot at the sides — therefore then it is like bent mavo; and therefore what Rambam wrote and some say specifically when there are ten amot — it is one view; rather more than ten amot:
27:_: And he shall make — Taz: Eruvin 10b; and see siman 362 — breached more than standing in the entire circumference is not partition; unlike in one wind — if the air of this side and that side is greater it annuls it; all that is less than four amot — if not, it does not annul it:
28:א: From within — Taz: all that has height nineteen and collects from within four amot — it is partition; and it is as if it does not exist; and likewise for enclosing the city so it is; and it will be explained in 365 in Magen Avraham section 9 and in other places it will be explained further:
28:ב: The poor man said I will record here words and the names mentioned in this siman with some explanation. Pasin: lechayim: tzurat hapetach: korah: (1) Pasin are (a) pas of the courtyard in seif 2 — four tefachim or two pasin mashehu from here and from here; and in what remains in the wall four require a tefach from here and from here. (b) Two pas width four amot in a mavo wider than twenty — the mavo explained here requires four amot specifically to be considered a mavo by itself; and then the air of this side and that side does not annul it; and even breached more than standing in a fourth wind does not annul it. (c) Pas four amot standing in the width of the mavo — it has no law of lechi by itself; but with intent it is lechi; but standing in the length of the wall of the mavo — even if placed for lechi it is annulled from the law of lechi even though recognizable as in seif 12 and 13 see there. (d) Pas in wells — even though breached more than standing — nevertheless since on each side an amah from here and from there it is properly partition nevertheless see Tosafos beginning of making pasin 17b and nevertheless the Merciful One concluded thus; and Eruvin section 17 section 27; and there is pas (5) in 365 that suffices with pas four tefachim such a case see there in Magen Avraham section 1 see there. (2) Three lechayim are: (a) lechi that permits a mavo breached in its entirety in ten amot — width has no measure and height nineteen; and valid from asherah wood; and should not distance from the wall of the mavo 3 tefachim as explained in seif 3 etc. I said to record here what is written on the side to the portion of Vayishlach see there and I will bury them under these terebinths in Shechem and in the name of our rabbi Rabbenu Bachya — gentile law is not in burial but scattering specifically is required; and in Rambam chapter 8 from gentiles how annulment — he crumbles or burns and casts into the sea; and see Yoreh De'ah siman 346 seif 64; and at the end of Temurah that it is not considered gentile that is not burned and buried — for scattering specifically is required and not burial; and there he said asherah wood forever forbidden — difficult, for in any case it is not burned; and one may say ashes are buried — perhaps rabbinically mashehu therefore so it is at the end of chapter 8 foundations of the Torah; and Pnei Yehoshua Pesachim unlike asherah wood mashehu — nevertheless fully adheres to your hand and one is lashed for benefit; and see Even HaEzer laws of kiddushin. And Taz letter 5; and in Tosafos Eruvin chapter 2 s.v. "but" — practical difference between the answers — reed above two reeds in tzurat hapetach — for answer one permitted and for two forbidden; and korah that he said there metal measure — somewhat difficult for answer two and for what Ran wrote in the name of Baal HaMaor Rosh Hashanah 29 — rabbinic mitzvot we say mitzvot are for benefit — difficult for lechi from asherah wood how permitted mashehu; or four partitions are required — nevertheless it is karmelit; and we hold that even rabbinically not for benefit as I wrote elsewhere. (b) Two lechayim in seif 4 in width four in the wall require a tefach — for in the wall itself there is no recognition in mashehu. (c) Lechi standing by itself in seif 11 — valid even a planted tree even less than a tefach; and siman 362 and 13. Tzurat hapetach — reed above asherah wood I explained above in disqualification of korah its law is explained. And lechi partition and one who throws to mavo is liable; and korah recognition and one who throws to mavo is exempt; and there was no time now to study properly — perhaps I will merit in the coming simanim to explain further:
